context_requirements: No annotated molecular targets for this class in the Drug Repurposing Hub
Known nematocide toxicity is organismal and reproductive (spermatogonial differentiation), not a direct transcriptional program in human somatic cell lines
No evidence that these nine human cell lines express the relevant reproductive/germline context
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in landmark gene expression at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines
Shared transcriptional signature across multiple lines that is not explained by vehicle or general toxicity
Enrichment of a specific pathway among changed landmark genes consistent with a direct drug-target interaction

evidence.supports: DBCP, a nematocide, causes prolonged oligo/azoospermia in rats by impairing spermatogonial differentiation rather than killing stem cells, indicating an organismal reproductive target rather than a general somatic transcriptional mechanism.
